title: Nobel Prize in Physics 2026: Francis Halzen awarded for work on cosmic neutrinos
content: Francis Halzen has received the Nobel Prize in Physics 2026 for his groundbreaking research at the IceCube Neutrino Observatory. This pivotal work has led to the discovery of high-energy neutrinos from cosmic sources, enhancing our comprehension of the universe. The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences recognizes his efforts with an award of 12 million Swedish kronor.

title: 'Wanted to tarnish image': Police on man held over AI poster showing cop assaulting woman
content: Delhi Police arrested a 24-year-old man named Nadeem Ahmed for creating a fake poster featuring a police officer. Police said the poster falsely depicted the officer sexually assaulting a woman during a protest, intending to damage police credibility. Investigators said Nadeem claimed to be an independent journalist and used AI tools for his misleading content.

title: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon has a ‘huge worry’ over US-China ‘big problems’
content: During a recent trip to Hong Kong, Jamie Dimon voiced his worries regarding geopolitical tensions potentially hindering economic growth between the U.S. and China. He stressed that maintaining robust growth is essential for resolving global conflicts. Engaging with local business leaders, Dimon called for practical collaboration among key nations and underscored the importance of addressing geopolitical risks that have drawn the attention of investors and policymakers worldwide.

title: Delaware homeowner wins court order in dispute over HOA records, maintenance
content: In a noteworthy court case, Gwendolyn Colston took on her community developer without legal representation and secured a favorable ruling. The Delaware Court of Chancery instructed the developer to ensure the upkeep of ponds and drainage systems in the area. Additionally, Colston gained access to insights on a contentious $44,329.

title: 'I have done my duty': Harmanpreet Kaur steps down as India captain
content: India women’s captain Harmanpreet Kaur has stepped down from captaincy in all formats, bringing an end to her stint as the team’s leader. Harmanpreet said the decision was not easy but felt she had fulfilled her responsibility as captain.

title: Saudi-backed Yemen forces claim key Red Sea strait secured
content: In a bold move to counteract Houthi insurgents, Saudi-backed Yemeni military forces have initiated Operation Yemen Dawn, bolstered by a coalition of 100 Saudi fighter jets. The offensive reportedly succeeded in reclaiming significant territories, including the strategic Dhubab airport and Mokha. However, the authenticity of these claims is yet to be independently verified, while the Houthis are challenging the narrative, asserting no losses and launching counterattacks on Saudi positions.

title: 99-million-year-old amber reveals insect with mouthpart twice its body length
content: A remarkable new insect species, Cretodorus noonoo, has been unearthed from 99 million-year-old amber found in Myanmar. This intriguing species is linked to the Neazoniidae family, renowned for its extraordinary mouthparts. These long and flexible adaptations reveal specialized feeding behaviors on tree sap. This discovery sheds light on the ecological interactions within Cretaceous forests, illustrating the diverse evolutionary strategies that shaped ancient ecosystems.

title: Florida mom rides 7,000 miles across 48 states, donates $17,560 to family support home
content: A Florida woman completed a 7,000-mile motorcycle journey across 48 states in six days. She raised $17,560 for Quantum House, an organization that supported her during her daughter’s hospital stay. The ride attracted attention, allowing her to create awareness about the organization. Jess's daughter, who benefitted from Quantum House, joined her when she presented the raised funds.

title: US Immigration authority makes filing of forms online mandatory
content: US Citizenship and Immigration Services plans to require online filing for many immigration forms soon. This process aims to improve efficiency and support national security. Applicants can choose to fill out forms online or upload completed PDFs. After submitting a form, users will receive a receipt notice and can track their case. Additional evidence can also be uploaded as the application is processed.

title: Why children touch a parent’s face while talking, according to psychology
content: Children frequently display physical affection towards their parents, such as gently touching their faces while talking. This interaction not only nurtures a sense of closeness but also helps them assess their parents' engagement. Studies indicate that such affectionate gestures are crucial for emotional growth throughout childhood. Parents must recognize the importance of these moments while also upholding appropriate boundaries to enhance emotional safety and deepen the parent-child relationship.

title: Bus conductor took his suitcase, it vanished: 11 years later, commission orders Rs 43k
content: The Uttarakhand state consumer commission found the bus conductor negligent for losing a passenger's suitcase. The passenger filed a complaint after his suitcase went missing on a Delhi-Dehradun bus journey in 2015. Initially awarded Rs 57,500, the compensation was reduced to Rs 25,000 when the passenger failed to prove actual costs. The transport corporation must pay Rs 43,000 in total compensation and litigation charges.

title: 19-year-old founder raises $11 million for $3,499 personal AI computer
content: At 19, Zain Javaid has raised $11 million to build Ghost, an AI hardware startup developing Core, a $3,499 personal AI computer. After abandoning a career in quantitative finance, Javaid became interested in AI agents that could understand users’ digital lives and act on their behalf. Core is designed to run AI models locally, bringing together data from computers, apps, wearables and smart-home devices while keeping personal information on the device, according to Ghost.

title: Kansas neighbour cut 133 trees; court upholds $6,500 damages award
content: A Kansas appeals court has upheld a $6,500 damages award against a man whose neighbour’s fence project led to 133 trees being cut on adjoining land in 2015. The court found the landowner filed his trespass case within the legal time limit and that there was enough evidence to hold Douglas Black responsible for the tree damage.

title: From Tokyo to Nagoya: Lovlina Borgohain’s long road to the top of the podium
content: Lovlina Borgohain clinched the 2026 Asian Games gold in boxing, upgrading her 2022 silver and becoming only the second Indian woman to win the title. Her journey, marked by Olympic success, setbacks, and resilience, culminated in an emotional win in Nagoya. The achievement also secured her a spot at the World Championships, underscoring her enduring significance in Indian boxing.

title: How Brittany Mahomes helped Patrick Mahomes stay grounded as an NFL star
content: Brittany and Patrick Mahomes have been an inseparable duo since their high school days, building a resilient bond over the years. Their relationship has been a cornerstone of Patrick's journey in the NFL, keeping him humble and focused amidst the spotlight. As proud parents of two children, they've gained a new appreciation for life and football.

title: South African tycoon plans $402m Formula 1 circuit on 600 hectares of farmland
content: Neal Froneman leads a consortium aiming to construct a $402 million Formula 1 circuit near Cape Town, marking a potential revival of South African motorsport after nearly 40 years. Currently in the pre-feasibility phase, the circuit is designed to accommodate 125,000 fans and will include a media complex and entertainment spots. If the endeavor succeeds, it could generate over 15,000 local jobs, enhancing tourism and the economy.

title: Why Bengal sculptors collect soil from Kolkata’s red-light area for Durga idols
content: Kumartuli, an iconic neighborhood in Kolkata, showcases the unique tradition of crafting Durga idols from clay. A significant aspect of this practice involves gathering soil from the thresholds of sex workers, which holds sacred meaning in Bengali heritage. This inclusion reflects a profound connection between faith and societal acceptance, stirring dialogue about purity and respect for all communities, particularly those often sidelined during significant cultural events like Durga Puja.

title: Why some parents still cover children’s books with brown paper
content: As schools reopen, many parents engage in the tradition of covering schoolbooks with brown paper. This activity provides a sense of organization and control during periods of uncertainty. Parents often express care through practical actions like preparing schoolbooks. The habit may also create a nostalgic connection between parents and their childhood experiences. Ultimately, this simple task can carry multiple layers of emotional significance for families.

title: Married in Rajouri, case filed in Jammu: why the high court let the divorce suit stay
content: A Jammu and Kashmir high court addressed the territorial jurisdiction of divorce suits amid allegations of cruelty. The wife's application for divorce was initially challenged by her husband based on the location of their marriage. The court found that part of the cause of action arose within its jurisdiction due to claims of cruelty. The husband's petition to transfer the case was dismissed for lacking merit.

title: Sikkim to get first train link by 2027; Rlys fast-tracks Rs 9,000 crore Gangtok line
content: The 44.5-km Sivok-Rangpo railway line is being constructed at an estimated cost of Rs 17,124 crore and will provide Sikkim with its first direct railway connection. The Rangpo-Gangtok line would serve as an extension of the railway network once the ongoing Sivok-Rangpo project, connecting Sivok in Darjeeling with Rangpo in East Sikkim, is completed.

title: Russia’s mystery ‘Iva’ missile: Is it Chinese or Iranian MANPADS system?
content: A man-portable air defense missile observed in Russian exercises has drawn attention for its possible origins. Analysts speculate it may be linked to Iranian or Chinese designs rather than Russian ones. The missile, referred to as 'Iva' by Russian personnel, resembles Iranian Misagh-3 and Chinese QW-series systems. Russia's existing arsenal includes advanced MANPADS systems aimed at low-flying threats.

title: Golfer paid $5 for green jacket; it later sold for $139,349
content: A golfer made a surprising find in 1994 when he bought a striking green jacket for only $5 at a Toronto thrift shop. To his amazement, it turned out to be a genuine Augusta National club jacket dating back to the 1950s. By 2017, this piece of history sold for an impressive $139,349 at auction, illustrating the escalating demand and skyrocketing prices for rare golf collectibles in today’s marketplace.

title: New Jersey oyster reefs cut storm wave height by up to 51%
content: A New Jersey project that began installing 40 constructed oyster reefs along about 800 metres of Gandy’s Beach in 2015 recorded more than 800 live oysters per square metre during early monitoring. Researchers also found the reefs reduced storm-wave height by up to 51% under certain conditions, though seven years of monitoring showed continued elevation and vegetation loss at the site.

title: Swatantra Bhardwaj gets bail in CJP assault case
content: A Delhi court granted regular bail to social media influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj, who was arrested over an alleged assault. Bhardwaj had previously received three weeks' interim bail under strict conditions related to his conduct. His detention followed a protest demanding his arrest due to comments made in an interview regarding the incident. He faced allegations of causing injury during the June protest and claimed political connections helped him evade justice.

content: The assessing officer made two major additions in this case. title: Bengaluru gym trainer ‘strangled’ by collagues at anniversary party
content: M Nandan, a 25-year-old gym trainer, was allegedly assaulted to death after a quarrel among trainers. The incident occurred at a flat in Kempapura following the gym's anniversary celebration. Police have arrested three suspects involved in the assault, which reportedly escalated after consuming drugs and alcohol. Nandan's mother filed a complaint, leading to the investigation and arrests.

title: Former bike mechanic turns discarded bicycles into prosthetic legs
content: Ben Hogan, once a bike mechanic, established Project Bike Leg with a vision to fabricate prosthetics from recycled bicycle components. His mission is to aid impoverished amputees worldwide who struggle to find affordable prosthetic options. Through engaging instructional videos on his website, Hogan empowers others to create their own bike legs.

title: Atlanta’s Presidential Hotel could become 282 apartments in $53.3m plan
content: DeKalb County has approved an initiative to transform the empty Presidential Hotel into modern market-rate apartments. This $53.3 million project will feature 282 residential units, including studio, one-bedroom, and two-bedroom layouts, with expected completion by the end of next year. Local residents have welcomed this development as a major enhancement to the community's housing options.

title: Chetan Bhagat says 4 focused work hours a day can be enough
content: Chetan Bhagat, speaking at the 18th Project Management South Asia Conference in Bengaluru, highlighted the significance of concentrated work. He suggested that only four hours of focused effort could lead to effective productivity, challenging the conventional belief that long hours equal high output. Bhagat connected work-life balance to overall happiness, advocating for personal needs, thus enriching the ongoing dialogue regarding ideal working hours in India.

title: Four nations, four drills, one month: How the army is expanding its military partnerships
content: India is currently conducting simultaneous military exercises with multiple nations to strengthen defense relationships. Exercise Yudh Abhyas with the United States focuses on high-altitude warfare, while Exercise Mountain Guardian involves the UAE in mountain operations. KAZIND with Kazakhstan and Nomadic Elephant with Mongolia also highlight India's growing military diplomacy. These activities improve interoperability and expose Indian troops to diverse military practices.

title: Teen leaves home for ‘1L PUBG task’, found asleep on bus 3 days later
content: A 14-year-old student left his home in Firozabad to complete a PUBG gaming task. His family reported him missing after he failed to return home. Police used CCTV footage and mobile tracking to locate him three days later in Indore. Officers reunited the boy with his family and urged parents to monitor children's online activities. Previous incidents of children leaving home for gaming tasks have occurred in other regions.

title: “My dad is relentless”: Meet Nobel winner Karl Deisseroth’s family and kids
content: Karl Deisseroth received the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for pioneering optogenetics. Following the announcement, he swiftly returned to his family routine by preparing sandwiches for his children. His wife, Dr. Michelle Monje-Deisseroth, was less surprised by the news due to Karl's work ethic. Their son, Alexander, and teenage children expressed pride in their father's achievement.

content: EC under fire as congress alleges 'mass manipulation and rigging' in polls . he demands accountability from chief election commissioner and other two election commissioners, prime minister and home minister . "more skeletons are tumbling out of the Election Omission of India's closet," he writes .

title: Harassment probe: ACP Vivek Bhagat opts out of Addl DCP charge 'of his own volition'
content: aCP Vivek Bhagat was promoted to the rank of Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police . he has sought withdrawal of the order assigning him the post . the order is being amended following an ongoing inquiry into allegations of sexual harassment .

title: Human remains found during $2.35m project at North Dakota governor’s residence
content: the location was once part of Bismarck’s first cemetery, which operated between 1873 and 1877 . a routine security upgrade at north Dakota’s governor’s residence turned into an archaeological investigation . months later, archaeologists have removed seven coffins containing human remains, along with an unidentified wooden box .
